summary: This program builds a library as an ArrayList of Book objects, prints them, and then demonstrates three more List methods: remove() to take a book off the shelf, contains() to ask whether a particular book is present, and isEmpty() to check whether the shelf has anything left on it.

lines.code: System.out.println("Total number of books after adding duplicate: " + books.size());
lines.text: Because a List allows duplicates, the second copy of The Hobbit really is stored, and the count rises to four — which is what makes the removal that follows worth watching closely.
remove() deletes only the first matching element, not every match, so donating one copy of The Hobbit leaves the other still on the shelf.
contains() compares the item you pass in against each element in the list and returns a boolean; here it is true because pride is the very same Book object that was added earlier.
isEmpty() states the question directly instead of writing size() == 0, and it reports false because books still remain after the removal.
